"""Convert a UTF-8 id,front,back CSV into a persistent Basic-card APKG."""
import argparse
import csv
from pathlib import Path

from ankiforge import BuildOptions, Note, Project


def build_csv(source: Path, destination: Path, namespace: str, deck: str) -> int:
    if destination.exists():
        raise ValueError('Choose a new output path; keep previously distributed APKGs')
    project = Project(namespace, default_deck=deck)
    seen = set()
    with source.open(encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='') as handle:
        rows = csv.DictReader(handle, strict=True)
        if rows.fieldnames != ['id', 'front', 'back']:
            raise ValueError('Expected the header id,front,back in that order')
        for row in rows:
            if None in row or any(value is None or not value.strip() for value in row.values()):
                raise ValueError(f'Line {rows.line_num}: expected three nonempty fields')
            key = row['id'].strip()
            if key in seen:
                raise ValueError(f'Line {rows.line_num}: duplicate id {key!r}')
            project.add(key, Note.basic(row['front'], row['back']))
            seen.add(key)
    if not seen:
        raise ValueError('The CSV must contain at least one note')
    project.build(BuildOptions.to(destination))
    return len(seen)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('source', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('destination', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--namespace', default='csv-vocabulary')
    parser.add_argument('--deck', default='Vocabulary')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    count = build_csv(args.source, args.destination, args.namespace, args.deck)
    print(f'{args.destination}: {count} notes, {count} Basic cards')

# Generate Anki flashcards with an AI assistant

Use an AI assistant to draft question-and-answer pairs from your notes, check
them against the source, then use Anki Forge to export an Anki `.apkg` deck.
Anki Forge is the open-source generation library in this workflow: the assistant
drafts content or writes a script, and your local Python, Node.js or Rust program
builds the cards.

You can [copy a coding-assistant brief](/#ai-quickstart) to get started with a
programming language, or follow the CSV workflow below. The website's brief
builder assembles text locally; it does not call an AI model or upload your notes.

<!-- section: choose-input -->
## Start with source material you can check

Use a short passage with a clear subject, such as your own course notes or a
vocabulary list. For PDFs, scans or lecture slides, extract and check the text
with a separate tool first. Anki Forge accepts the content you provide through
its APIs; PDF extraction and OCR are outside this library.

Keep each proposed question focused on one fact. Include enough context for the
answer to make sense when the card appears outside the original document.

<!-- section: draft-cards -->
## Ask for CSV cards

Paste this example into your assistant. Replace the source passage when making
your own deck, and adjust the requested note count and IDs for your new notes:

```text
Turn the source below into exactly three Basic Anki notes.
Use only facts stated in the source. Do not add facts from memory.
Each question must test one fact and be understandable on its own.
Return only UTF-8 CSV with the header id,front,back, with no Markdown fence.
Use the IDs es:hola, es:gracias and es:adios for these three vocabulary items.
Quote any CSV field containing a comma, quote or newline correctly.

Source:
In Spanish, hola means hello, gracias means thank you, and adiós means goodbye.
```

The expected content is equivalent to:

```csv
id,front,back
es:hola,hola,hello
es:gracias,gracias,thank you
es:adios,adiós,goodbye
```

The assistant may phrase the front differently. Check each row against the source,
remove ambiguous or unsupported answers, then save the reviewed result as
`cards.csv`. Assign each new note a unique ID and retain it during later edits;
do not ask the assistant to regenerate IDs for an existing deck.

<!-- section: export-apkg -->
## Turn reviewed cards into an APKG

Follow [CSV to Anki with Python](csv-to-anki.md) for the complete program,
installation commands and sample input. That script checks the CSV shape,
requires unique IDs and writes a persistent package. The sample creates three
Basic cards with no media.

If your data is already JSON or you need images and audio, use the
[JSON to Anki recipe](json-to-anki.md), with complete Python, Node / TypeScript
and Rust programs. CSV and JSON are parsed by your application before it passes
notes to Anki Forge.

For help writing a custom program, use the
[coding-assistant brief](/#ai-quickstart) and describe the input fields, desired
card type and output filename. The [optional Anki Forge Skill](ai-assistants.md)
provides the public API references and task workflows for assistants that load Skills.

<!-- section: check-result -->
## Check the cards before studying

Open the generated APKG in Anki and inspect the card count, question, answer and
formatting. For the CSV example, expect three notes and three cards in the Spanish
deck. A successful export confirms that a package was built; it does not establish
that an AI's answers are correct or useful for studying.

For fill-in-the-blank questions, use [Cloze cards](cards.md). For diagram labels,
use [Image Occlusion](image-occlusion.md) with the image and mask coordinates you
provide; this does not automatically detect labels in an image.

Keep the original distribution APKG for the next release and follow the
[update workflow](updates.md). Preserve the namespace and note IDs, inspect the
comparison, and account for Anki's import settings and newer local edits.

# Convert CSV to Anki flashcards with Python

Turn a vocabulary spreadsheet into an Anki `.apkg` file with Python and Anki
Forge. This example reads a UTF-8 CSV with `id`, `front` and `back` columns,
creates Basic question-and-answer cards, and exports a deck you can share.
Python's standard-library CSV parser reads the spreadsheet; Anki Forge builds
the package. Exporting does not require Anki to be installed.

For a one-off spreadsheet import, Anki already supports
[delimited text files](https://docs.ankiweb.net/manual/importing/text-files).
Use this recipe when you want a repeatable script, your own note IDs and a
distributable APKG. An Excel `.xlsx` file must first be saved as UTF-8 CSV.

<!-- section: prepare-csv -->
## Prepare the CSV

Save this as `cards.csv`, or [download the sample](/generated/recipes/csv-to-anki/cards.csv):

<!-- source: docs/recipes/csv-to-anki/cards.csv -->
```csv
id,front,back
es:hola,hola,hello
es:gracias,gracias,thank you
es:adios,adiós,goodbye
```
<!-- /source -->

Keep the header exactly as shown and use commas as separators. Quote fields
containing commas, double quotes or line breaks using
[CSV quoting rules](https://docs.python.org/3/library/csv.html).
The script accepts a UTF-8 byte-order mark, as some spreadsheet exports include one.
It rejects duplicate IDs, missing values, extra columns and empty input.

Assign an ID once and keep it when the question or answer changes. Do not derive
IDs from a row's position or editable card text. Use a different namespace for
unrelated datasets; keep the namespace stable for successive versions of this deck.

<!-- section: install -->
## Install Anki Forge

Use ordinary CPython 3.11 or later on a
[supported platform](compatibility.md). Create and activate a virtual environment:

```sh
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ankiforge==0.3.1
```

On Windows, activate with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.
No spreadsheet library or AI service is needed for this conversion.

<!-- section: convert -->
## Generate the APKG

Save the following as `csv_to_anki.py` beside `cards.csv`, or
[download the script](/generated/recipes/csv-to-anki/csv_to_anki.py):

<!-- source: bindings/python/examples/csv_to_anki.py -->
```python
"""Convert a UTF-8 id,front,back CSV into a persistent Basic-card APKG."""
import argparse
import csv
from pathlib import Path

from ankiforge import BuildOptions, Note, Project


def build_csv(source: Path, destination: Path, namespace: str, deck: str) -> int:
    if destination.exists():
        raise ValueError('Choose a new output path; keep previously distributed APKGs')
    project = Project(namespace, default_deck=deck)
    seen = set()
    with source.open(encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='') as handle:
        rows = csv.DictReader(handle, strict=True)
        if rows.fieldnames != ['id', 'front', 'back']:
            raise ValueError('Expected the header id,front,back in that order')
        for row in rows:
            if None in row or any(value is None or not value.strip() for value in row.values()):
                raise ValueError(f'Line {rows.line_num}: expected three nonempty fields')
            key = row['id'].strip()
            if key in seen:
                raise ValueError(f'Line {rows.line_num}: duplicate id {key!r}')
            project.add(key, Note.basic(row['front'], row['back']))
            seen.add(key)
    if not seen:
        raise ValueError('The CSV must contain at least one note')
    project.build(BuildOptions.to(destination))
    return len(seen)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('source', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('destination', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--namespace', default='csv-vocabulary')
    parser.add_argument('--deck', default='Vocabulary')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    count = build_csv(args.source, args.destination, args.namespace, args.deck)
    print(f'{args.destination}: {count} notes, {count} Basic cards')
```

<!-- /source -->

Run it from that directory:

```sh
python csv_to_anki.py cards.csv vocabulary-v1.apkg --namespace spanish-vocabulary --deck Spanish
```

The sample produces `vocabulary-v1.apkg` with **three notes and three Basic
cards** in the **Spanish** deck, with no media. It prints:

```text
vocabulary-v1.apkg: 3 notes, 3 Basic cards
```

Choose an output path that does not exist. The script refuses to replace a
previous file so you can retain the original distribution package.

<!-- section: verify-and-extend -->
## Import, check and extend

Open `vocabulary-v1.apkg` in Anki. Check that the deck contains `hola → hello`,
`gracias → thank you` and `adiós → goodbye`; preview the cards and verify accents.
Check the content before distributing it, especially if an AI drafted the CSV.

This recipe creates text-only Basic cards. For other workflows:

- [AI-assisted Anki card generation](ai-anki-cards.md): draft and review CSV rows from source notes.
- [JSON to Anki](json-to-anki.md): use Python, Node / TypeScript or Rust, package images and audio, and review a second release.
- [Basic and Cloze cards](cards.md): choose question-and-answer or fill-in-the-blank cards.
- [Update generated Anki decks](updates.md): use the previous original APKG as an update baseline and inspect the comparison.

For a later release, preserve the namespace and note IDs and follow the update
workflow before publishing. Stable IDs help identify notes; Anki's import
settings and newer local edits still affect updates.

让 AI 助手根据笔记起草问题和答案，对照原文审核后，再用 Anki Forge 导出 Anki

```text

In Spanish, hola means hello, gracias means thank you, and adiós means goodbye.
```

```csv
id,front,back
es:hola,hola,hello
es:gracias,gracias,thank you
es:adios,adiós,goodbye
```

助手可能采用不同的问题表述。请逐行对照原文，修正含糊或缺少依据的答案，再保存为
`cards.csv`。新笔记使用唯一 ID，之后编辑时保持不变；不要让助手为已有牌组重新生成 ID。

## 将审核后的卡片导出为 APKG

[用 Python 将 CSV 转为 Anki](csv-to-anki.md)提供完整程序、安装命令和输入示例。
脚本检查 CSV 格式和 ID 唯一性，生成持久保存的包。示例包含 3 张 Basic 卡片，不含媒体。

如果已有 JSON 数据，或需要图片与音频，可使用 [JSON 转 Anki 教程](json-to-anki.md)，

再将笔记传给 Anki Forge。

需要助手编写自定义程序时，复制[编程助手任务说明](/#ai-quickstart)，补充输入字段、
卡片类型和输出文件名。支持加载 Skill 的助手还可以使用
[Anki Forge Skill](../ai-assistants.md)，读取公开 API 参考与任务流程。

<!-- section: check-result -->
## 学习前检查卡片

在 Anki 中打开生成的 APKG，检查卡片数量、问题、答案和排版。CSV 示例应在 Spanish
牌组中生成 3 条笔记和 3 张卡片。成功导出说明包已生成，并不代表 AI 的答案已经核实，
或适合作为学习材料。

填空题可以使用 [Cloze 卡片](cards.md)。图表标注可以使用
[图片遮挡](image-occlusion.md)，由你提供图片和遮挡坐标；它不会自动识别图中的标签。

保留原始分发 APKG，后续版本按[更新流程](updates.md)操作：保持命名空间和笔记 ID，
检查比较结果，并考虑 Anki 导入设置与较新的本地编辑。

笔记保存字段；笔记类型及其模板把字段转换成卡片。牌组在 Anki 中组织生成的卡片。[核心概念](/docs/concepts/)说明这些关系、Project 的值所有权和稳定身份。

## 构建下一项功能

- [CSV 转 Anki](/docs/csv-to-anki/)：用 Python 将词汇表批量生成 APKG。
- [JSON 转 Anki](/docs/json-to-anki/)：用三种开发语言生成带媒体的卡片，并检查更新。
- [AI 辅助制卡](/docs/ai-anki-cards/)：根据笔记起草卡片，核对答案后导出 APKG。
- [Basic 与 Cloze](/docs/cards/)：创建问答和填空卡片。
- [图片与音频](/docs/media/)：注册真实资源并附加到卡片。
- [自定义笔记类型](/docs/custom-notetypes/)与[模板包](/docs/templates/)：定义字段、布局与 CSS。
- [图片遮挡](/docs/image-occlusion/)：根据图像区域创建问题。
- [更新与分发](/docs/updates/)：在版本之间传递身份和修订证据。

卡片类型指南使用可运行的 Rust 示例，CSV 教程使用 Python，JSON 教程覆盖三种开发语言。
Node 和 Python API 页面说明相应接口及其差异。

## 查找答案与参与贡献

操作失败时参考[排查问题](/docs/troubleshooting/)，运行环境支持和客户端导入条件见[已验证环境](/docs/compatibility/)。

# 用 Python 生成 Anki APKG

创建并激活虚拟环境，然后安装[公开 PyPI 包](https://pypi.org/project/ankiforge/)：

```sh
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ankiforge==0.3.1
```

Windows 使用 `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` 激活。使用普通 CPython 3.11 或更高版本及匹配的平台 wheel；已有发布检查覆盖 CPython 3.11–3.14，参见[已验证环境](../compatibility.md)。

## 导出牌组

将以下程序保存为 `main.py`：

<!-- source: bindings/python/examples/quickstart.py -->
```python
from ankiforge import Project, Note, BuildOptions

project = Project('spanish', default_deck='Spanish')
project.add('es:hola', Note.basic('hola', 'hello'))
output = project.build(BuildOptions.to('spanish.apkg'))
print(output.artifact.path)
```
<!-- /source -->

```sh
python main.py
```

在 Anki 中打开持久保存的 `spanish.apkg`，其中 **Spanish** 牌组包含 **hola → hello**。后续编辑时保持命名空间 `spanish` 和笔记键 `es:hola` 不变。导出不需要安装 Anki。

## 继续学习

已有词汇表时，参考 [CSV 转 Anki](csv-to-anki.md)。需要根据原始笔记起草卡片时，
可从 [AI 辅助制卡](ai-anki-cards.md)开始。

完整媒体与更新任务见 [JSON 到 Anki](../json-to-anki.md#python)。

- [图片与音频](../media.md)及 [Python 媒体 API](../python/api.md#media-and-occlusion)
- [自定义笔记类型](../custom-notetypes.md)和[模板包](../template-bundles.md)
- [图片遮挡](../image-occlusion.md)
- [比较与更新](../updates.md)
- [Python API](../python/api.md)及[诊断](../python/diagnostics.md)
- [从 genanki 迁移](../python/genanki-migration.md)

原生源码编译见[源码构建](../source-builds.md)。

Use it when your learning content lives in code or structured data and you want to rebuild and distribute decks repeatedly. ## Start with your language Install a public package and export your first deck; choose your entry point. | Language | First result | Continue | | --- | --- | --- | | Rust | Run the first-deck example | Add to your application | | Node / TypeScript | Install and build your first deck | API and async behavior | | Python | Install and export a deck | API and output ownership | Prefer to see the result first? Explore the card examples and download their generated packages. ## Understand the pieces A note holds fields; a note type and its templates turn those fields into cards. Decks group the resulting cards in Anki. The core concepts explain these relationships, owned Project values, and stable identity. ## Build your next feature - CSV to Anki: turn a vocabulary spreadsheet into an APKG with Python. - JSON to Anki: generate cards with media and review an update in three languages. - AI-assisted card generation: draft cards from your notes, review the answers and export an APKG. - Basic and Cloze: create question/answer and fill-in-the-blank cards. - Images and audio: register real assets and attach them to cards. - Custom note types and template bundles: define fields, layouts and CSS. - Image Occlusion: create questions from regions of an image. - Update and distribute: carry identity and revision evidence between releases. Card-type guides use runnable Rust examples; the CSV recipe uses Python and the JSON recipe covers all three languages. Node and Python API pages explain their corresponding interfaces and any differences. ## Find answers and contribute Use troubleshooting when an operation fails, and verified environments for runtime support and client import conditions. Anki Forge is licensed under MIT. Report reproducible issues on GitHub, or read the contributor guide.
